decision: D115 §一.4 and §三 — the JavaScript the Node target emits, including the three Worker realms and the stdin child it ships as source text, is real source that the JavaScript parser checks, not a template literal nothing can lint.

constants.name: VELAR_NODE_ENV_RUNTIME
documentation: * `velar/env` — the canonical Node environment boundary. The process.env
* object and every JavaScript operation used to validate and read it are
* captured while the official module initializes, so later application-Realm
* replacement cannot redirect environment reads or execute accessors.

constants.name: VELAR_NODE_FILESYSTEM_RUNTIME
documentation: * The canonical application-facing filesystem boundary. Validation, UTF-8 and
* immutable Velar values stay in this Realm; all Node fs effects run through
* the private isolated velar/node-host-v1 runtime dependency.

constants.name: VELAR_NODE_FS_MODULE_SOURCE
documentation: /** `velar/fs` — the filesystem boundary over the compiler's UTF-8 runtime. */

constants.name: VELAR_NODE_HOST_RUNTIME
documentation: * `velar/host` — the canonical Node lifecycle boundary. It captures the signal,
* exit, timer, Promise and diagnostic operations it uses before application
* code can replace their public properties or prototypes.

constants.name: VELAR_NODE_HTTP_RUNTIME
documentation: /** `velar/http` — the outbound HTTP client over the isolated Node host. */

constants.name: VELAR_NODE_HOST_STATIC_FILE_SOURCE
documentation: * The static-file half of the privileged Node serve transport, its own file so
* that both halves stay inside D115 §一.1's reading budget: path
* canonicalization inside a root, the file load with its fallback,
* ETag/Last-Modified/Range conditionals, and the ranged write. It is one
* contiguous region of the same Worker source, composed back at exactly the
* position it occupied.

constants.name: VELAR_NODE_HOST_WORKER_SOURCE
documentation: * The privileged Node transport shared by the official Node standard modules.
* This Worker loads only compiler-owned source and static Node built-ins;
* VelarScript application code and npm dependencies remain in the application
* Realm.

constants.name: VELAR_SHARED_NODE_HOST_RUNTIME
documentation: * `velar/node-host-v1` — the application-facing proxy for the shared privileged
* Node worker, carrying that worker's source as the string it constructs it
* from. This module is a private compiler-extension dependency and has no
* VelarScript interface.

constants.name: VELAR_NODE_PATH_MODULE_SOURCE
documentation: /** `velar/path` — bounded path arithmetic, with no filesystem effect at all. */

constants.name: VELAR_PROCESS_HOST_RUNTIME
documentation: * The canonical host-intrinsic boundary shared by the Node and Desktop targets
* of velar/process. It is compiler-extension infrastructure, not a public Velar
* module: target runtimes inline it before accepting application or bridge
* values so later JavaScript prototype replacement cannot change validation.

constants.name: VELAR_PROCESS_GROUP_SIGNAL_RUNTIME
documentation: * Signalling one owned process group and confirming it is gone: the pair the
* `velar/process` owner Realm reclaims a crashed Worker's children with. The
* policy above it — how many attempts, how long between them, when to give up —
* stays with the reaper in the target's own module text.
* It is composed in after the owner state it reads (`__velarNodeProcessKill`,
* `__velarNodeProcessNativeProcess`, `__velarNodeProcessPlatform`), which is why
* it is a run of that module rather than a module of its own.

constants.name: VELAR_NODE_PROCESS_WORKER_SOURCE
documentation: * The complete Node-only process host. It is evaluated in an eagerly
* initialized Worker realm that never loads application dependencies, because
* Node's own child_process implementation consults public EventEmitter/stream
* prototypes while spawning and cannot be made post-initialization-stable in a
* shared application realm by wrapping only the outer calls.

constants.name: VELAR_NODE_PROCESS_MODULE_SOURCE
documentation: * `velar/process` — the owner Realm: validation, handles, the reaper, and the
* isolated worker's source as the string it is constructed from.

constants.name: VELAR_NODE_SERVE_LISTENER_RUNTIME
documentation: * The listener adapter: the half of `velar/serve` that speaks to a Node
* `http.Server` directly, for `velar/websocket.listen({http: app})` and for a
* low-level `serve(handler)`. Its own file so that both halves stay inside D115
* §一.1's reading budget — it is one contiguous region of the emitted module,
* composed back at exactly the position it occupied.
* It answers the same refusals the privileged host transport answers, in the
* same wire form (SV-I1), because an application must not be able to tell which
* transport is under it from the shape of a 404.

constants.name: VELAR_NODE_SERVE_TEST_RUNTIME
documentation: * The `velar/server-test` client, its own file so that both halves of
* `velar/serve` stay inside D115 §一.1's reading budget. It is one contiguous
* region of the emitted `velar/serve` module — `velar/server-test` reaches it
* through `ServeApp.__velarCompilerBridge.testClient` — composed back at exactly
* the position it occupied.

constants.name: VELAR_NODE_SERVE_PREFIX
documentation: * `velar/serve` above the route-shape rule it closes over. The application-facing
* contract: HTTP sockets, request streams, backpressure and static-file effects
* live in the shared isolated Node host, and this Realm owns only Velar values,
* handlers and strict JSON/type boundaries.

constants.name: VELAR_NODE_SERVE_BODY
documentation: /** `velar/serve` below the route-shape rule: routing, the listener, the test client. */

constants.name: VELAR_NODE_SERVER_TEST_MODULE_SOURCE
documentation: /** `velar/server-test` — the test client, reached through the serve bridge. */

constants.name: VELAR_NODE_TERMINAL_INPUT_SOURCE
documentation: * Owns the inherited stdin handle and forwards it to the worker over IPC. The
* last record it sends is the one the worker waits for, so it must survive the
* channel teardown that follows it.

constants.name: VELAR_NODE_TERMINAL_WORKER_SOURCE
documentation: * The isolated terminal host. The Worker never loads application code or
* packages; an on-demand child owns the inherited stdin handle so a blocking
* pipe read is cancellable without exposing application-Realm stream prototypes.

constants.name: VELAR_NODE_TERMINAL_RUNTIME
documentation: * The application-facing proxy for the isolated terminal host, carrying that
* host's source as the string it constructs it from. It captures all validation,
* MessagePort and Worker operations before application code runs; stdin
* ownership, decoding, and fd writes live in the worker.

constants.name: VELAR_NODE_TERMINAL_MODULE_SOURCE
documentation: /** `velar/terminal` — the terminal proxy over the compiler's UTF-8 runtime. */

constants.name: VELAR_NODE_WEBSOCKET_RUNTIME
documentation: /** `velar/websocket` — frames, connections and the upgrade path over `velar/serve`. */

constants.name: VELAR_NODE_WORKER_RUNTIME
documentation: /** `velar/worker` — the worker pool, its cancellation protocol and backpressure. */
